name: Exact RAM size
plain: Only a capped RAM figure exists; exact memory is hidden.
meaning: deviceMemory returns 0.25 to 8 GB (capped, Chromium, secure context, power of two rounding), so a 64 GB workstation looks like 8. Firefox and Safari expose nothing. Memory pressure is not readable.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit
fields.range: heap limit, Chromium, hints at RAM class

limits.headline: Can't see your exact RAM size; only a rounded number capped at 8 GB
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads in Chrome or Edge

limits.differs: Chrome and Edge share a capped number. Firefox and Safari share nothing.

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot see your exact memory. They get a capped, rounded number at best.

marketing.name: Navigator.deviceMemory
marketing.pitch: Docs explain that the value is rounded and capped, so it only hints at memory.

story.for_you: A 64 GB workstation looks like an 8 GB laptop to a website. Firefox and Safari share nothing at all. Your exact memory stays private.
story.for_makers: Exact memory would be a precise device clue and a wealth signal. The web caps and rounds it, which still lets sites pick a light or heavy page. That is enough for performance but not for precise tracking.

use_cases.example: A browser game wanted exact RAM for texture choices and uses the capped hint plus a quick speed test.
A browser design tool wanted real memory to warn about huge files and relies on error handling.
A video call app wanted exact RAM to plan background blur and watches performance instead.
An ad vendor wanted exact RAM to guess income and sees only the capped number.
A fraud tool wanted exact RAM to spot virtual machines and uses other signals.
A web app team wanted real memory for crash reports and logs the capped value.
A big spreadsheet app wanted exact RAM and instead loads data in chunks.

risks: Capped number still hints at a device tier

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
